recommendation.recommendation: Conduct a comprehensive field inspection and immediately improve soil organic matter with organic amendments.
recommendation.justification: The crop is currently thriving (NDVI 0.75) under optimal temperature, humidity, and soil pH, but low soil organic carbon and low SAVI indicate a risk of future fertility loss and moisture stress. Prompt inspection will catch any emerging disease or pest pressure, and organic inputs will restore soil health, protecting yield and profitability.
actions: 1. Perform a systematic walk‑through of the mango orchard to check for anthracnose, powdery mildew, fruit‑fly activity, and visual signs of nutrient deficiency (leaf chlorosis, stunted growth).
2. Record GPS‑tagged observations and photograph any suspect symptoms for expert review.
3. Collect soil samples from 5–7 representative points (0–30 cm depth) for laboratory analysis of organic carbon, nitrogen, and pH.
4. Apply well‑composted organic matter or mature manure at 8 t ha⁻¹ (or 2 t acre⁻¹) and incorporate lightly into the topsoil to raise organic carbon toward the ‘high’ requirement.
5. Maintain the existing drip‑irrigation schedule (every 7–10 days) and verify emitter performance to avoid over‑ or under‑watering.
6. Update the farm management log with inspection results, soil test request, and amendment dates.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil organic carbon will improve nutrient retention and water‑holding capacity, reducing root‑zone stress. Early disease/pest detection will enable timely control, preserving the high canopy vigor and supporting a profitable mango harvest in the May‑July window.
monitoring_plan: • Weekly visual scouting for disease and pest symptoms until the next flowering stage.
• Re‑measure NDVI and SAVI via satellite or drone imagery 30 days after amendment to verify canopy health and soil exposure.
• Repeat soil organic carbon test 3 months post‑application to confirm target increase.
• Track irrigation volumes and soil moisture sensors (if available) to ensure adequate moisture during the fruiting phase.
• Monitor market prices weekly and adjust sales strategy to the identified best market (Kanyakumari Uzhavar Sandhai).

steps.finding: Conduct a comprehensive field inspection and immediately improve soil organic matter with organic amendments.
actions: 1. Perform a systematic walk‑through of the mango orchard to check for anthracnose, powdery mildew, fruit‑fly activity, and visual signs of nutrient deficiency (leaf chlorosis, stunted growth).
2. Record GPS‑tagged observations and photograph any suspect symptoms for expert review.
3. Collect soil samples from 5–7 representative points (0–30 cm depth) for laboratory analysis of organic carbon, nitrogen, and pH.
4. Apply well‑composted organic matter or mature manure at 8 t ha⁻¹ (or 2 t acre⁻¹) and incorporate lightly into the topsoil to raise organic carbon toward the ‘high’ requirement.
5. Maintain the existing drip‑irrigation schedule (every 7–10 days) and verify emitter performance to avoid over‑ or under‑watering.
6. Update the farm management log with inspection results, soil test request, and amendment dates.
